name: Cache Storage
plain: A store of HTTP responses used by service workers to serve pages offline.
meaning: Lets a site keep its own pages, scripts and API responses on the device. Shares the origin quota with IndexedDB. Opaque cross-origin responses are padded in quota accounting so sites cannot probe sizes.

access.persistence: Until cleared or evicted. Safari 7 day cap applies
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep copies of pages and files so the site opens without internet
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you visit or install the site.
can: Save pages, images and data for later
Serve them when you are offline
cannot: Keep data for ever, since the browser may delete it when disk space is low
Hold more than the site's storage limit

story.what_it_is: A store of web responses that lets a site work offline and load fast.

marketing.name: Service workers and caching
marketing.pitch: Google pitches caching with service workers so web apps load fast and work without a connection.

marketing.name: CacheStorage
marketing.pitch: Documents the store pages use to keep copies of web files for offline use.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why a web app opens quickly even on a bad connection, and why some pages still work on a plane.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to make web apps feel like phone apps. Fast starts keep people from leaving. It also uses your storage space and can hold old copies of a site.

use_cases.example: A browser game keeps its art and sound files here, so it starts fast and can run offline.
A social web app opens its shell at once and then loads new posts.
A coffee or store web app lets you browse the menu without a connection.
A document or note app opens offline and syncs when you reconnect.
A music or podcast web app keeps pages and covers ready for a quick start.
A news site saves recent stories so you can read them in a tunnel.
A web boarding pass keeps working with no signal.

technical_bounds: Opaque responses are padded (Chrome pads to about 7 MB each in quota accounting)

abuse: Persisting tracker scripts on the device
